checks.name: Animation honours reduced-motion
checks.command: node -e "const fs=require('fs'),path=require('path');let css='';for(const d of ['Styles','UI']){if(!fs.existsSync(d))continue;for(const f of fs.readdirSync(d,{recursive:true})){if(f.endsWith('.css'))css+=fs.readFileSync(path.join(d,f),'utf8')}}const animates=/(^|[;{\s])(animation|transition)\s*:/.test(css);const guarded=/@media\s*\(prefers-reduced-motion:\s*reduce\)/.test(css);if(animates&&!guarded){console.error('CSS animates but has no prefers-reduced-motion guard');process.exit(1)}console.log('Motion respects prefers-reduced-motion')"

cannotTest: Most of this rule is judged, not matched. Not decidable by regex or command: whether forms order fields logically, focus the right control, validate inline, mark required fields, show useful placeholders/tooltips, auto-populate reliably, and stay usable by keyboard, pointer and touch; whether tooltips are reachable by Tab/Enter on touch and by assistive technology; whether the prediction kernel/adapter split is respected, adapter resolution is predictable, confidence is genuinely calibrated, learning updates correctly ignore invalid entries, and suggestions never overwrite explicit values or interfere with typing or submission; whether the 80%/50% thresholds are applied consistently in real prediction code (no prediction engine exists in this repository, so the shared-kernel logic is unexercised); whether the theme is cohesive and centrally applied beyond colour and font-family placement; and whether the interface is modern, friendly, warm, polished, non-patronising and free of manipulative engagement or gratuitous motion. The reduced-motion command only proves that some prefers-reduced-motion block exists when CSS animates; it cannot verify that every animation and transition is actually covered. Positive tabIndex is treated as the detectable symptom of unpredictable focus order, but focus behaviour itself is not simulated.
